name: ooptdd-ouroboros-protocol
purpose: Deterministically reduce one OOPTDD evidence generation and seal structurally and semantically conformant receipts within configured ordinary-progress and lineage bounds.
rationale: The stable need is a pure protocol kernel and receipt contract, not an independently operated service.
No durable single-writer, scheduler, daemon, or recovery owner exists in this repository today.
Caller-owned ports preserve a promotion path without fabricating runtime guarantees.

boundary.owns: Immutable protocol values, deterministic transition selection, identity rules, receipt validation, and conservative legacy upcasting
boundary.mechanism: step(snapshot, typed_event) returns a new snapshot plus stable effect intents or an observable rejection
policy_outside: How tests and mutations are executed
Scheduling, retries, no-progress limits, approvals, invocation limits, and operational timeout values
boundary.state_authority: The caller owns persistence and concurrency; the module owns only an immutable value transition

contract: step(CycleSnapshot, ProtocolEvent) -> TransitionResult; receipt_from_snapshot(terminal_snapshot) -> receipt/v2; successor_from_receipt(validated_superseded_receipt) -> CycleSnapshot
invariants: Identical snapshot and event values produce an identical transition result.
An exact cycle-scoped event replay cannot advance accepted history and re-emits only stable effect IDs.
Within one cycle, one event ID cannot denote two intents.
Every event binds the full cycle ID, generation, and predecessor-hash identity through cycle_identity_sha256.

All phase runs have distinct run IDs and artifact namespaces; each records the phase-appropriate executed source, including the mutated source for the negative run and the locked baseline for the other roles.
No terminal state retains an active mutation.
Every Bite finding has exactly one disposition before sealing.
A bound-material change supersedes the generation and names a distinct successor.
SEAL never launches a successor; successor construction is downstream of generated and validated predecessor-receipt identity.
A complete receipt trace carries replayable accepted event envelopes and their phase edges.
failure_model: Malformed or out-of-order input yields a typed rejection and audit intent without ordinary state mutation.
Identity conflict fails closed; if a mutation is active, restoration is required before termination.
Accepted-history budget exhaustion halts ordinary progress but reserves restoration as a safety action; invalid or replayed calls require caller-owned invocation and no-progress bounds.
Infrastructure uncertainty is inconclusive, never silently translated into evidence absence.
verification: Transition tests cover the complete cycle, forbidden ordering, replay, conflict, interruption, restoration, and Bite succession.
Identity tests pin exact-byte hashing, canonical-object hashing, Unicode behavior, and domain separation.
Receipt tests tamper with authoritative fields and show v1 upcasts remain incomplete.
Machine-readable FSM traces cover every declared transition, guard-false branch, and invalid-event policy.
promotion_gates: At least two current adapters require the same stable orchestration contract.
A durable single writer must own snapshots, an outbox, recovery, and schema migration.
Independent operations require backpressure, cancellation, and observability across process boundaries.
falsifiers: If consumers need incompatible lifecycle policy, keep adapter-specific runners around the shared reducer.
If no durable operational owner appears, do not promote this module into an engine.
If the receipt cannot discriminate a seeded protocol defect, its completeness claim is invalid.
